💻 DISK SCHEDULING (FCFS)

Question:
Consider a disk queue with requests for I/O to blocks on cylinders:
98, 183, 37, 122, 14, 124, 65, 67

Using FCFS (First Come First Served) scheduling, find the total number of head movements, if the initial disk head position is 53.

Options:
(A) 640
(B) 620
(C) 630
(D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above


Answer:
(A) 640


Explanation:
FCFS → Requests are processed in the same order as given.

Total Head Movement = Σ |Current Position − Next Request|

Initial Head = 53

53 → 98  = |98 - 53|  = 45
98 → 183 = |183 - 98| = 85
183 → 37 = |37 - 183| = 146
37 → 122 = |122 - 37| = 85
122 → 14 = |14 - 122| = 108
14 → 124 = |124 - 14| = 110
124 → 65 = |65 - 124| = 59
65 → 67  = |67 - 65|  = 2

Total = 45 + 85 + 146 + 85 + 108 + 110 + 59 + 2 = 640


Quick Points:
- FCFS follows given order (no sorting)
- Always take absolute difference
- Include first movement (initial → first request)

--------------------------------------------------
1. BASICS
--------------------------------------------------
→ Disk Scheduling = Order of servicing I/O requests
→ Only ONE request is served at a time (others wait in queue)
→ Also called I/O Scheduling

Total Overhead Movement = Total Head Movement
= Total distance covered by the disk arm

--------------------------------------------------
2. FORMULAS
--------------------------------------------------
Disk Access Time
= Seek Time + Rotational Latency + Transfer Time

Total Seek Time
= Total Head Movement × Seek Time (per track)

--------------------------------------------------
3. PERFORMANCE METRICS
--------------------------------------------------
→ Seek Time → Time taken to move the disk head
→ Rotational Latency → Time taken for the required sector to rotate under the head
→ Transfer Time → Time taken to read/write data

--------------------------------------------------
4. GOALS
--------------------------------------------------
✔ Minimize Seek Time
✔ Maximize Throughput
✔ Minimize Latency
✔ Ensure Fairness

--------------------------------------------------
5. ALGORITHMS + NUMERICALS
--------------------------------------------------

1. FCFS (First Come First Serve)
→ Requests are served in arrival order
→ No starvation
→ High seek time

Numerical

Queue = 50, 82, 170, 43, 140, 24, 16, 190
Head = 50

Total Head Movement

|82−50| + |170−82| + |43−170| + |140−43| + |24−140| + |16−24| + |190−16|

= 32 + 88 + 127 + 97 + 116 + 8 + 174

Total = 642 tracks

--------------------------------------------------

2. SSTF (Shortest Seek Time First)
→ Serve the nearest request first
→ Fast
→ Starvation possible

Numerical

Queue = 82, 170, 43, 140, 24, 16, 190
Head = 50

Service Order
50 → 43 → 24 → 16 → 82 → 140 → 170 → 190

Total Head Movement

|50−43| + |43−24| + |24−16| + |82−16| + |140−82| + |170−140| + |190−170|

= 7 + 19 + 8 + 66 + 58 + 30 + 20

Total = 208 tracks

--------------------------------------------------

3. SCAN (Elevator Algorithm)
→ Move in one direction, then reverse

Numerical

Head = 50
Direction = Higher
Disk End = 199

Total Head Movement

(199 − 50) + (199 − 16)

= 149 + 183

Total = 332 tracks

--------------------------------------------------

4. C-SCAN (Circular SCAN)
→ Move only in one direction
→ After reaching the end, jump to the beginning

Numerical

Total Head Movement

(199 − 50) + (199 − 0) + (43 − 0)

= 149 + 199 + 43

Total = 391 tracks

--------------------------------------------------

5. LOOK
--------------------------------------------------
→ Similar to SCAN, but stops at the last request (does not go to disk end)

Numerical

Total Head Movement

(190 − 50) + (190 − 16)

= 140 + 174

Total = 314 tracks

--------------------------------------------------

6. C-LOOK
--------------------------------------------------
→ Similar to C-SCAN, but jumps from the last request to the first request

Numerical

Total Head Movement

(190 − 50) + (190 − 16) + (43 − 16)

= 140 + 174 + 27

Total = 341 tracks

--------------------------------------------------
6. EXAM TIPS
--------------------------------------------------
✔ Always use absolute difference | |
✔ Count every head movement
✔ Initial head position must be included
✔ Direction is important in SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK and C-LOOK
✔ FCFS always follows the given order

--------------------------------------------------
FINAL REVISION
--------------------------------------------------
Total Overhead Movement
= Total Head Movement
= Sum of all head movements (tracks)

│   │   │
│   │   ├── Example:
│   │   │   ├── h(k) = k mod 5
│   │   │   ├── Insert → 10, 15, 20

│   │   ├── Example:

│   │   │   ├── Insert → 10, 15
│   │   │

The Divide and Conquer algorithm consists of three main steps:

1. DIVIDE

1. Divide the array into two halves

mergeSort(arr, l, r)

      mergeSort(arr, m+1, r)

Quick sort is a divide-and-conquer algorithm that partitions the array around a pivot and recursively sorts the subarrays.

1. Choose a pivot (first / last / random / median)
2. Partition the array so that:
• left of pivot < pivot
• right of pivot > pivot
3. Recursively apply quick sort on left and right subarrays

quickSort(arr, low, high)
   if low < high
      pi = partition(arr, low, high)
      quickSort(arr, low, pi - 1)
      quickSort(arr, pi + 1, high)

Question:
Consider a relation with schema R(P, Q, R, S, T) and the FD set {PQ → R, R → S, S → P}. How many superkeys does relation R contain?

Solution:

Given FDs:
PQ → R
R → S
S → P

Step 1: Identify mandatory attributes

Q and T never appear on the RHS of any FD.

Therefore, Q and T must be present in every candidate key and superkey.

Step 2: Find candidate keys

PQT⁺:
P, Q, T → R → S
Therefore, PQT is a candidate key.

QRT⁺:
Q, R, T → S → P
Therefore, QRT is a candidate key.

QST⁺:
Q, S, T → P
P, Q → R
Therefore, QST is a candidate key.

Candidate Keys:
PQT, QRT, QST

Step 3: Count Superkeys

Every superkey must contain Q and T and at least one of P, R, S.

Number of non-empty subsets of {P, R, S}:

2³ − 1 = 7

Superkeys:
1. PQT
2. QRT
3. QST
4. PQRT
5. PQST
6. QRST
7. PQRST

Answer:
7 Superkeys

Shortcut:
Q and T are compulsory.
Choose any non-empty subset from {P, R, S}.

Number of Superkeys = 2³ − 1 = 7
